clue.text: Foreign counterpart of White House in romantic movie

definitions.meaning: the Spanish for a white house, casa meaning house and blanca white
the 1942 Bogart and Bergman wartime romance set in Morocco

explanation.surface: A film buff notes a foreign twin of the President's residence in a love story.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' is only a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The city name is literally Spanish for 'white house', and it titles the classic Bogart romance.

clue.text: End of arm used to deliver blow

definitions.meaning: the band at the end of a sleeve, which sits at the wrist
a light slap or smack with the hand

explanation.surface: A boxer's fist at the end of the arm delivers a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the end piece of a sleeve and a slap given with the open hand.

clue.text: One wretched student initially turned up for information on courses

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
bally is a mild British euphemism for bloody, so wretched or confounded

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of student

explanation.surface: A miserable student looks up details of the courses on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses I + BALLY + S (IBALLYS) to give the answer; BALLY is dated British slang for 'blasted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Syllabuses (plural of syllabus) set out what each course of study will cover.

clue.text: Cause financial problem, as current expansion may

definitions.meaning: to cost more than one can afford
a river current swelling in flood may burst through its banks

explanation.surface: Something that causes money trouble, just as an expanding current might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like it means present-day money supply, but it is a river's flow, and the bank is the riverside.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means costing too much, and literally describes floodwater bursting a riverbank.

clue.text: Get these looking into fraud, it seems?

definitions.text: Get these looking into fraud, it seems

indicators.note: looking into the following words finds the letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Someone investigating a fraud would naturally order these checks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking into' tells you the answer is concealed in 'fraud, it seems'; the whole clue also describes the answer, since these checks are what fraud investigators call for.
explanation.definitionFit: Official inspections of accounts are the checks ordered when financial fraud is suspected.

clue.text: Raised road as matter of principle to consider in hearing

parts.note: a cause is a principle or movement one supports

indicators.note: in hearing signals that a word is spoken and another spelling is entered

parts.note: to weigh something up is to consider it

explanation.surface: A road is built up as a matter of principle, to be considered at a public hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in hearing' looks like a planning inquiry, but it signals that WEIGH is said aloud and entered as WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A causeway is a road built up on an embankment across wet ground or water.

clue.text: Violently strike against big contract

definitions.meaning: to hit or shut with great force
in bridge a ... is a contract to win all or all but one of the tricks

explanation.surface: Someone lashes out angrily at a large business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' suggests business, but it is a bridge bid; 'against' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means hitting hard and also names the biggest bids in bridge.

clue.text: Politically progressive bill modified over long time

indicators.note: in a down clue the anagrammed letters sit over and around the inserted piece
modified means the letters of bill are changed into a new order

parts.note: an era is a long period of history

explanation.surface: A forward-looking bill is amended after a long delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like a parliamentary bill, apt for politics, but it is just anagram fodder; 'over' is the container signal, apt in a down clue where one piece sits around another.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal politics favour reform and individual freedom, a broadly progressive stance.

clue.text: Follow suit with thrust that may secure victory in court

definitions.text: that may secure victory in court

parts.note: to match is to do the same as another, like following suit at cards
the thrust of an argument is its main point

explanation.surface: A fencer copies the opponent and lunges, hoping to win the bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a law court, but it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, the point that would win the whole match is called this.

clue.text: One's never affected by this French craze

definitions.text: One's never affected by this French craze

parts.words: One's never affected by this French craze
parts.note: a French term for a delusion shared by a pair of people, so a single person alone cannot have it

explanation.surface: A French mania that, oddly, never strikes anyone on their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' reads as 'a person', but the point is that this madness needs two sufferers.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means 'madness for two', a psychiatric delusion shared by two close people.

clue.text: From Latin and French, translated to be helpful

parts.note: ab is the Latin preposition meaning from
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: Translating from Latin and French turns out to be useful.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to aid or assist someone, chiefly in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Uncommunicative inclination of officers reappearing in emergency

definitions.note: the definition names the officers, the answer the register that holds them

parts.note: a reserved person keeps their thoughts to themselves
a list is a lean or tilt, as of a ship

explanation.surface: Some taciturn officers have a tendency to resurface when a crisis strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; the definition describes the people on the register.
explanation.definitionFit: A register of retired armed-forces officers who can be called back to serve in an emergency.

clue.text: Corrupt racketeer harms study of consumer needs

indicators.note: corrupt means the letters of the following words are spoiled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A crooked racketeer damages a survey of what shoppers want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' looks like an adjective for the racketeer but shuffles RACKETEER HARMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Firms commission this kind of research to learn what customers want and will buy.

clue.text: Page relating to joints going into detail

parts.note: articular is the anatomical adjective for joints

explanation.surface: A page about joints goes into detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going into' is a link here, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular is a single item or detail, as in 'the particulars of the case'.

clue.text: Get out or in

definitions.meaning: to step down from a vehicle
a fire that is still in is burning, still lit

explanation.surface: A two-word puzzle offering the choice of leaving or staying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' has to be read as 'still burning', like a fire that is in.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means getting off a vehicle and also on fire, as a fire that is still in is.

clue.text: Terminal defeat

definitions.meaning: Napoleon's final defeat, so a decisive downfall

explanation.surface: A last defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminal' looks like an adjective meaning final, but it is a noun: a rail station.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a London rail terminus, and 'meeting one's Waterloo' means suffering final defeat.

clue.text: Rambling to a pub is what gives townies a taste of rural life

definitions.text: what gives townies a taste of rural life

indicators.note: rambling means the letters wander out of their order

explanation.surface: City dwellers get a sense of the countryside by walking to a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling' looks like country walking, but it shuffles TO A PUB IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A coined word for sprawling suburbs that give townspeople a diluted idea of the countryside.

clue.text: Digital signal successfully received

definitions.meaning: a gesture made with the thumbs, which are digits
a phrase saying a message or plan got through or won approval

explanation.surface: A digital transmission gets through without a hitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' looks like electronic data, but it refers to fingers and thumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising a thumb is a hand gesture of approval or success.

clue.text: Find 'fault with dearer decorative tape

parts.note: prices that are up are higher, so dearer
braid is woven trimming used to decorate uniforms

explanation.surface: Someone complains about pricier ornamental ribbon.
explanation.definitionFit: To upbraid is to scold or reproach someone for a fault.

clue.text: Writer — left diary, finally appearing, and still around

indicators.note: around means the first piece goes around the others

parts.note: even is used as in 'even better', meaning still

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of diary

explanation.surface: An author leaves a diary which eventually turns up and is still in circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: John Evelyn was a famous 17th-century English diarist. 'around' puts L and Y inside EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: John Evelyn was a seventeenth-century English author best known for his diary.

clue.text: Opening in theatre of the old school

definitions.meaning: cutting open a boil or abscess, as a surgeon does in an operating theatre
... College is an English public school in Sussex, someone's old school

explanation.surface: A traditional first night at the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests the stage, but it is an operating theatre; Lancing is a fee-paying school in Sussex, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means piercing to open a boil and is also the name of a well-known English school.

clue.text: Uproar resulting from shift of one line in Europe's capitals

indicators.note: moving one stroke from one capital letter to another changes both letters
in the capitals the stroke lands in the P, which with an extra leg becomes R

parts.note: the word Europe written in capital letters

explanation.surface: A row follows when a railway line is moved across the European capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: Write EUROPE in capitals and take the bottom stroke off the first E, making F, and add it to P, making R: FURORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A furore is an outburst of public anger or excitement, a commotion.

clue.text: Dining at pub, editor shortly moved on to cold dessert

indicators.note: on to means the rearranged letters are attached after the first piece

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: moved means the letters of these words are shifted into a new order

parts.note: ed is the short form of editor

explanation.surface: Dining at a pub, an editor quickly moves on to a chilled pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' is the anagram signal, and 'on to' sets the shuffled letters after the C; the surface's moving on to dessert hides both jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabinet pudding is a traditional British steamed or chilled pudding of sponge, dried fruit and custard.

clue.text: Part of elementary education singled out for heavy blow

parts.note: singled out suggests just one
the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are basic schooling, so one R is part of it

explanation.surface: One part of basic schooling is picked out for harsh punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'three Rs' (reading, writing, 'rithmetic) are the basics of primary education.
explanation.definitionFit: A oner is British slang for a hard punch, one that needs only one blow.

clue.text: Idle head

definitions.meaning: ..., from ... of bread, is rhyming slang for head

explanation.surface: A lazy boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use your loaf' is British rhyming slang (loaf of bread = head).
explanation.definitionFit: The word means lazing about and, in British rhyming slang, the head.

clue.text: Rejected concession I offered in choice, for parliamentary group

indicators.note: in means the following pieces go inside the word for choice

parts.note: an option is a choice

indicators.note: rejected means the word for concession is thrown back, read backwards

parts.note: a sop is a small concession made to placate someone

explanation.surface: A rejected compromise is offered as an option to a party in parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' reverses the concession word, and 'in' puts it with I inside the choice; 'offered' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In parliament, the main parties not in government are called the Opposition.

clue.text: Fish that's pink, apart from the tail

indicators.note: apart from the tail means drop the final letter of the word for pink

parts.note: ruddy means reddish or pink, like a healthy complexion

explanation.surface: A pinkish fish without its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart from the tail' removes the Y from RUDDY.
explanation.definitionFit: The rudd is a European freshwater fish of the carp family with red fins.

clue.text: Questions place of rapid economic development as supposed threat

parts.note: an exam paper is a set of questions
a tiger economy is a fast-growing country, such as those of East Asia

explanation.surface: Exam questions put to a booming economy as a perceived danger.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper tiger is something that seems threatening but is actually powerless.
